_comment: What this harness relies on in Claude Code, and nothing else.
upstream-check.sh fails (exit 1) when one of these stops being true, and the daily
run hands that to Claude to fix. It does not assess what a release adds.
expected_default_mode is the permission mode config/settings.json ships; the check
fails if the two disagree or the CLI stops accepting it. memory_index_limits are
the thresholds memory-lint and memory-verify enforce, read out of the CLI on each
run rather than assumed. The hook events to check come from config/settings.json.
The two thresholds that decide how much of MEMORY.md is loaded, read out of
the CLI rather than assumed. They were folklore here for a while: this repo's
own research doc recorded '~200-line index cap is unsubstantiated', while
memory-verify and memory-lint both enforced 200 as fact. Both turned out to
be right about the number and wrong about the confidence.
Upstream destructures {trimmed, lineCount, byteCount} and tests
lineCount > <lines> and byteCount > <bytes>. The size limit is BYTES -- the
identifier is literally byteCount -- which is why this harness reports bytes.
Truncation is line-first: the index is cut to <lines> lines, then clamped to
<bytes>, so passing line 200 drops everything after it.
Section 5 of the check re-extracts both numbers by name, so a minifier rename cannot
strand the check the way a hardcoded identifier would.
